Create a Chebyshev grid

Source: R/chebyshev.R
chebknots.Rd

Create a Chebyshev grid on a hypercube.

Usage

chebknots(dims, intervals = NULL)

Arguments

dims

The number of grid points in each dimension. For Chebyshev polynomial of degree dims-1.

intervals

A list of vectors of length 2. The lower and upper bounds of the hypercube.

Value

An array of dimension dims. The Chebyshev grid points.

Details

If intervals is not provided, it is assumed that the domain of the function in each dimension is [-1, 1]. Thus, standard Chebyshev knots are produced. If dims is of length 1, intervals may be a vector of length 2 rather than a list with a vector of length 2.

Examples

# Standard knots for degree 3
chebknots(4)
#> [[1]]
#> [1]  0.9238795  0.3826834 -0.3826834 -0.9238795
#> 
# Knots in the interval [2,3] for degree 3
chebknots(4, intervals = c(2, 3))
#> [[1]]
#> [1] 2.961940 2.691342 2.308658 2.038060
#> 
# Multivariate knots
chebknots(c(x = 3, y = 4, z = 3))
#> $x
#> [1]  0.8660254  0.0000000 -0.8660254
#> 
#> $y
#> [1]  0.9238795  0.3826834 -0.3826834 -0.9238795
#> 
#> $z
#> [1]  0.8660254  0.0000000 -0.8660254
#> 
# Multivariate grid
head(expand.grid(chebknots(c(x = 3, y = 4, z = 5), list(c(1, 3), c(4, 6), c(800, 900)))))
#>          x        y        z
#> 1 2.866025 5.923880 897.5528
#> 2 2.000000 5.923880 897.5528
#> 3 1.133975 5.923880 897.5528
#> 4 2.866025 5.382683 897.5528
#> 5 2.000000 5.382683 897.5528
#> 6 1.133975 5.382683 897.5528
